extracted.intended_audience: general literate public; readers and writers interested in literary taste, poetry, and visual art criticism
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts of prescriptive and evaluative statements about poetry, painting, and character-representation—guidance on what makes a work moving, well-made, or blameworthy. Useful for writers, critics, and readers assessing artistic merit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simplicity and naturalness over artifice
rubrics_metrics.description: This Song is a plain simple Copy of Nature, destitute of the Helps and Ornaments of Art... because the Sentiments appear genuine and unaffected, they are able to move the mind of the most polite Reader.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Valuing a plain, natural copy of life: sincere sentiment and unaffected presentation can move readers more than elaborate artifice. Critics and writers should recognise that simplicity may be a virtue and not dismiss works for 'mean' language when the feelings are genuine.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incidents should grow out of the subject
rubrics_metrics.description: The Incidents grow out of the Subject, and are such as are the most proper to excite Pity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Narrative events ought to arise naturally from the premise/subject of the piece; contrived or extraneous incidents weaken emotional effect. For tragic or moving tales, select incidents that naturally elicit the intended feeling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genuine sentiment and unaffected expression
rubrics_metrics.description: The Thoughts ... are natural, and therefore cannot fail to please those who are not Judges of Language, or those who... have a true and unprejudiced Taste of Nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authenticity of feeling is a key criterion: honest, unforced emotions trump rhetorical show. Even technically rough verse can succeed if its emotional truth is palpable.

rubrics_metrics.name: A small poetic ornament can be effective
rubrics_metrics.description: As for the Circumstance of the Robin-red-breast, it is indeed a little Poetical Ornament; and to shew the Genius of the Author amidst all his Simplicity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minor, well-chosen poetic touches (symbolic or small images) can enhance a simple tale and reveal authorial imagination without spoiling the work's naturalness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language deficiencies can be outweighed by natural thought
rubrics_metrics.description: Though the Language is mean... the Thoughts ... are natural and therefore cannot fail to please.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not equate polished diction with intrinsic merit; prioritize truthful thought and feeling. Editors/readers should judge whether poor phrasing conceals or undermines genuine sentiment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use physical appearance (the air of the face) to reveal character
rubrics_metrics.description: We may be better known by our Looks than by our Words... the Air of the whole Face is much more expressive than the Lines of it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For characterisation, show inward dispositions through outward mien and bearing: the general 'air' or expression conveys temperament and feeling more effectively than isolated facial lines or dialogue alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Every passion gives a cast to the countenance — show passions via small features
rubrics_metrics.description: Every Passion gives a particular Cast to the Countenance, and is apt to discover itself in some Feature or other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use subtle, specific physical details (a brow, an eye, an expression) to indicate emotional states; these micro-observations make characters believable and allow readers to infer interior life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid Vanity — superficial, uniform smirking or fashionable affectation
rubrics_metrics.description: VANITY... All the Faces he drew were very remarkable for their Smiles, and a certain smirking Air... All his Men were Petits Maitres, and all his Women Coquets. The Drapery... made up of all the glaring Colours that could be mixt together.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beware creating characters or styles that are uniformly fashionable, shallow, or smirking; such superficial affectation flattens variety and reduces credibility. In style, avoid excessive ornamentation that only signals fashion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid slavish copying (Stupidity)
rubrics_metrics.description: A laborious Workman... copied after him. He was dressed like a German, and had a very hard Name, that sounded something like STUPIDITY.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mindless imitation of prevailing fashions or of another artist's manner is a fault. Encourage originality and critical distance rather than mechanical copying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid Fantasque — grotesque distortion without purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: FANTASQUE... He had an excellent Hand at a Chimera, and dealt very much in Distortions and Grimaces... the most elaborate of his Pieces was at best but a terrifying Dream; agreeable Monsters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Excessive eccentricity or grotesque distortion that does not serve a coherent artistic purpose can produce only spectacle or terror and fail to create meaningful art. Fantasy should be balanced by intelligibility and emotional purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid Avarice — hasty, unfinished work
rubrics_metrics.description: AVARICE... his hasty Hand... left his Pictures so unfinished, that the Beauty in the Picture... faded sooner than in the Person after whom it was drawn. He made so much haste... that he neither gave himself time to clean his Pencils, nor mix his Colours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rushed composition and failure to complete and polish work leads to ephemeral or flawed outcomes. Take adequate time for craft, revision, and finishing touches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value Industry — meticulous attention to detail
rubrics_metrics.description: INDUSTRY... If he drew the Portraiture of a man, he did not omit a single Hair in his Face; if the Figure of a Ship, there was not a Rope among the Tackle that escaped him.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Diligent, painstaking attention to realistic detail produces verisimilitude and technical excellence. Thoroughness in observation and execution is a virtue in both visual and verbal art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid Envy — destructive over-retouching or excessive criticism
rubrics_metrics.description: ENVY... His Pencil aggravated every Feature that was before over-charged, loaded every Defect, and poisoned every Colour it touched... though he produced no Originals of his own.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Over-editing or constantly amplifying faults (or critics who only magnify defects) can spoil otherwise good work. Editing should aim to clarify and improve, not to accentuate flaws for their own sake.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value Time and mellowing — restraint and gradual refinement improve works
rubrics_metrics.description: TIME... his Pencil was so very light... he wore off insensibly every little disagreeable Gloss... He also added such a beautiful Brown to the Shades, and Mellowness to the Colours, that he made every Picture appear more perfect than when it came fresh from the Master's Pencil.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowing work to age, mature, and be revisited with a light, patient hand can improve tone and depth. Revision, restraint, and the passage of time can enhance subtlety and harmony.
